title: Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell Detection
content_md: Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell detection is harder than it looks, because the vulnerability is not confined to one product. Node2Shell, also called HTTP2Shell, is CVE-2026-111497: an out-of-bounds write in Google’s Brotli C decoder, versions 1.0.3 to 1.2.0, scored CVSS 4.0 9.2. Since the flaw sits in a shared compression library, it reaches Node.js, Python Brotli packages, Bun, curl, Envoy, and other software that decodes Brotli. This article covers Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell detection using a log sample analyzed in LogTotal, a log analysis tool that matches events to known threats. Below, we cover the vulnerability context, the log source, what LogTotal reported, and how to respond. Get Started For Free Node2Shell (HTTP2Shell) Analysis The vulnerable code sits in Brotli C decoder versions 1.0.3 to 1.2.0. Google, as the numbering authority, scored it 9.2 under CVSS 4.0, while Node.js rates it High. To read the log sample correctly, it helps to know how the bug is triggered, how the disclosure unfolded, and which software versions and configurations are exposed. Vulnerability details for Node2Shell A Brotli stream that declared a single block type and then switched blocks was not rejected, so decoding continued in an invalid state and wrote past a buffer. Any process that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data can be hit, in two directions: Inbound: a crafted Brotli-compressed HTTP request body sent to a server that decodes it.
